hooks.command: python3 -c "import json,sys,os; d=json.load(sys.stdin); fp=(d.get('tool_input') or {}).get('file_path',''); root=os.environ.get('CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR') or os.getcwd(); rel=os.path.relpath(os.path.normpath(os.path.join(root,fp)),root) if fp else ''; rel=rel.replace(os.sep,'/'); members={'CLAUDE.md':'claude','.github/copilot-instructions.md':'copilot','CONTRIBUTING.md':'detail'}; which=members.get(rel) or ('detail' if rel.startswith('architecture/') else None); tail=' First check the rule belongs in an always-loaded file at all: if a CI test already enforces it, neither mirror should carry it.'; msgs={'claude':'You edited CLAUDE.md - MIRROR RULE: .github/copilot-instructions.md carries the same rules for a reviewer. If this change is a RULE rather than detail-only wording, make the equivalent change there before calling it done. These two move together or not at all; the CI check fails a one-sided edit.','copilot':'You edited .github/copilot-instructions.md - MIRROR RULE: CLAUDE.md carries the same rules for an implementer. If this change is a RULE rather than detail-only wording, make the equivalent change there before calling it done. These two move together or not at all; the CI check fails a one-sided edit.','detail':'You edited '+rel+' (the detail layer) - this is the correct home for detail, and a detail-only edit rightly touches nothing else, so there is usually nothing more to do. Only if you have written a RULE does it need promoting into CLAUDE.md AND .github/copilot-instructions.md together.'}; msg=(msgs[which]+tail) if which else ''; print(json.dumps({'hookSpecificOutput':{'hookEventName':'PostToolUse','additionalContext':msg}})) if which else None"
